title: A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks
author_affiliations: IBM Research Laboratory, San Jose, California
keywords: relational model; data banks; data independence; relational algebra; normal forms; database architecture
abstract: Future users of large data banks must be protected from having to know how the data is organized in the machine. A model of data based on n-ary relations, a normal form for data base relations, and the concept of a universal data sublanguage are introduced. In contrast to existing tree-structured or network-structured models, the relational model provides a means of describing data with its natural structure only.

local_path: data/A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks.pdf
notes: Foundational paper introducing the relational data model.

title: System R: Relational Approach to Database Management
authors: M. M. Astrahan; M. W. Blasgen; D. D. Chamberlin; K. P. Eswaran; J. N. Gray; P. P. Griffiths; W. F. King; R. A. Lorie; P. R. McJones; J. W. Mehl; G. R. Putzolu; I. L. Traiger; B. W. Wade; V. Watson

keywords: System R; relational DBMS; SQL; concurrency control; recovery subsystem; query compilation; locking
abstract: System R is a database management system which provides a high level relational data interface. The system provides a high level of data independence by isolating the end user as much as possible from underlying storage structures. The system permits definition of a variety of relational views on common underlying data, authorization, integrity assertions, triggered transactions, logging, and recovery.

title: The Volcano Optimizer Generator: Extensibility and Efficient Search
author_affiliations: Portland State University; University of Colorado at Boulder
venue_name: IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering
keywords: query optimization; Volcano optimizer; extensible query evaluation; dynamic programming; rule-based optimization; physical algebra
abstract: Emerging database application domains demand not only new functionality but also high performance. To satisfy these requirements, the Volcano project provides efficient, extensible tools for query and request processing. One of these tools is a new optimizer generator translating data model, logical algebra, physical algebra, and transformation rules into optimizer source code using directed dynamic programming.

title: Query Optimization
keywords: query optimization; search space; cost models; relational algebra; dynamic programming; randomized algorithms
abstract: Given a query, there are many access plans that a database management system can follow to process it and produce its answer. All plans are equivalent in terms of final output but vary drastically in cost. This survey outlines the primary components of modern query optimizers: the search space of algebraic expressions, cost estimation models, and search algorithms including dynamic programming and randomized heuristics.

keywords: B-trees; indexing; access methods; concurrency control; logging; query processing
abstract: Modern B-Tree Techniques summarizes the state of the art in B-tree implementation, focusing on scalable concurrency control, high-performance latching, transactional logging, cache-conscious node sizing, prefix and suffix compression, and efficient support for batch insertions and index maintenance in contemporary database architectures.

title: Towards a Robust Query Optimizer: A Principled and Practical Approach
venue_name: ACM SIGMOD Conference on Management of Data
keywords: robust query optimization; risk management; cardinality estimation; plan choice; error estimation
abstract: Research on query optimization has focused almost exclusively on reducing query execution time, while qualities such as consistency and predictability have largely been ignored. We explore how query optimization can be made more robust, focusing on minimizing risk caused by estimation errors in cardinality. We present formal models and practical algorithms that choose robust execution plans.

title: The R*-tree: An Efficient and Robust Access Method for Points and Rectangles
authors: Norbert Beckmann; Hans-Peter Kriegel; Ralf Schneider; Bernhard Seeger
author_affiliations: University of Bremen; University of Bremen; University of Bremen; University of Bremen
venue_name: ACM SIGMOD Conference on Management of Data
keywords: R*-tree; spatial indexing; multidimensional access methods; bounding rectangles; range query; nearest neighbor
abstract: The R-tree, one of the most popular access methods for rectangles, is based on heuristic optimization of the area of the enclosing rectangle in each inner node. We present the R*-tree which incorporates a combined optimization of area, margin, and overlap of each enclosing rectangle in the directory. Exhaustive experiments demonstrate performance gains up to 50 percent for spatial queries.

title: A Survey of Top-k Query Processing Techniques in Relational Database Systems
authors: Ihab F. Ilyas; George Beskales; Mohamed A. Soliman
author_affiliations: University of Waterloo; University of Waterloo; University of Waterloo
keywords: top-k; query processing; rank-aware processing; relational databases; scoring functions
abstract: Efficient processing of top-k queries is a crucial requirement in many interactive environments involving massive data. In this survey, we classify top-k processing techniques in relational databases across query models, access methods, implementation levels, data certainty, and supported scoring functions, contrasting rank-aware query operators with traditional relational operators.

title: The Google File System
authors: Sanjay Ghemawat; Howard Gobioff; Shun-Tak Leung
author_affiliations: Google, Inc.; Google, Inc.; Google, Inc.
venue_name: ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles
keywords: Google File System; distributed file system; chunkserver; fault tolerance; high throughput; append-only
abstract: We have designed and implemented the Google File System, a scalable distributed file system for large distributed data-intensive applications. It provides fault tolerance while running on inexpensive commodity hardware, and it delivers high aggregate performance to a large number of clients. The design reflects a marked departure from earlier file system assumptions by optimizing for large streaming reads and concurrent appends.
notes: Underlying storage foundation for MapReduce and Bigtable.

title: MapReduce: Simplified Data Processing on Large Clusters
venue_name: USENIX Symposium on Operating Systems Design and Implementation
keywords: MapReduce; parallel processing; fault tolerance; cluster computing; large-scale data; distributed systems
abstract: MapReduce is a programming model and an associated implementation for processing and generating large data sets. Users specify a map function that processes a key/value pair to generate a set of intermediate key/value pairs, and a reduce function that merges all intermediate values associated with the same intermediate key. The run-time system automatically parallelizes execution across large clusters and handles machine failures.

authors: Fay Chang; Jeffrey Dean; Sanjay Ghemawat; Wilson C. Hsieh; Deborah A. Wallach; Mike Burrows; Tushar Chandra; Andrew Fikes; Robert E. Gruber

title: Dremel: Interactive Analysis of Web-Scale Datasets
authors: Sergey Melnik; Andrey Gubarev; Jing Jing Long; Geoffrey Romer; Shiva Shivakumar; Matt Tolton; Theo Vassilakis
author_affiliations: Google, Inc.; Google, Inc.; Google, Inc.; Google, Inc.; Google, Inc.; Google, Inc.; Google, Inc.

abstract: Dremel is a scalable, interactive ad-hoc query system for analysis of read-only nested data. By combining multi-level execution trees and a columnar representation for nested records, it runs aggregation queries over petabyte-scale datasets in seconds. The system scales to thousands of CPUs and petabytes of user data, complementing MapReduce-based batch computation.

title: Inverted Indexes for Phrases and Strings
authors: Manish Patil; Sharma V. Thankachan; Rahul Shah; Wing-Kai Hon; Jeffrey Scott Vitter; Sabrina Chandrasekaran
author_affiliations: Louisiana State University; Louisiana State University; Louisiana State University; National Tsing Hua University; The University of Kansas; Louisiana State University
venue_name: ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
keywords: inverted index; phrase search; string search; index compression; suffix trees; text retrieval
abstract: Inverted indexes are fundamental data structures in information retrieval. For each unique word occurring in a document collection, the inverted index stores a list of document occurrences. In terms of string documents where word boundaries are undefined or for phrase queries, standard indexes incur quadratic storage or redundancy. We introduce inverted indexes that work naturally and compactly for strings and phrase search.
datasets_used: Pizza and Chili Corpus; TREC Disks 4 and 5
notes: Core text search index structure for full-text queries.

abstract: Information retrieval has witnessed profound transformation from classical lexical inverted index architectures to modern neural rankers and dense vector representations. This survey systematically reviews recent advances in text retrieval, query expansion, neural passage ranking, multilingual search, and multimodal integration, discussing open challenges in efficiency and scalability.
